subject: general
question: What is a key factor considered in the World Happiness Report's ranking?
solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP per capita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Happiness Report ranks countries based on various indicators that reflect the well-being of their citizens, one of the most important being **GDP per capita**.
 
• **GDP per capita** measures the average income of a country's citizens and serves as a strong indicator of economic prosperity and living standards.
 
• This metric is closely linked to the ability of individuals to access basic necessities, healthcare, education, and other resources contributing to happiness.
 
• The World Happiness Report utilizes GDP per capita as a key variable to gauge material well-being, which directly impacts overall life satisfaction.
 
• Countries with higher GDP per capita often rank higher due to better infrastructure, higher standards of living, and improved social services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Military Strength**

 
 
• While military strength is important for national security, it is **not a direct determinant of happiness**.
 
• Countries with strong military capabilities might not necessarily have high happiness levels as national defense does not inherently affect individual well-being or quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Internet Speed**
 
 
• Internet speed, though important for connectivity and communication, is not a core factor in the World Happiness Report.
 
• While faster internet can improve efficiency and access to resources, it does not directly measure a population's happiness or satisfaction with life.
 
 
 
• **Forest Cover**
 
 
• Forest cover contributes to environmental sustainability and has indirect effects on happiness through improved air quality and mental health benefits.
 
• However, it is not a primary metric used in the World Happiness Report rankings.
 
 
 
• **World Happiness Report**
 
 
• The World Happiness Report is published annually by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
 
• It ranks countries based on six main factors: **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption**.
 
• The report emphasizes both economic and non-economic factors in determining happiness, providing a holistic measure of a country's well-being.
